task_text: Continue from the requirements in docs/. The next slice is undecided.

requirements_read.quote: The first board exports one SVG from local data.
Editing is requested, but its interaction style is undecided.

proposed_scope.summary: Deliver exactly what line 1 names and no more: a module that loads one board description from a local file (plain JSON, since no other format is specified anywhere in docs/), exports it as one SVG document, and is tested. Editing is prepared only as library operations (add/move/set-fill on the loaded board) because line 2 requests editing but explicitly leaves 'its interaction style' undecided — no interface, no UI, no persistence of edits back to the file is built.
deliverables: library editing operations on board (no interaction layer)
proposed_scope.explicitly_not_included: any editing UI or CLI (interaction style undecided, line 2), write-back of edits to the local data file (not requested by any line)

key_decision_question: Does 'local data' mean a file format that edits must write back into, or just an in-repo/on-disk read-only source — i.e., when a user edits the board in a later slice, where do the edits live?

options.title: Local data is a JSON file loaded at start; edits stay in memory for the session
options.description: loadBoard reads JSON from disk once; building edits happen in memory; nothing is written back in this slice.
options.tradeoff: Fully matches line 1 with no assumptions beyond 'local data reads from somewhere local'; export is one-shot as required — but edited boards are lost on restart unless a later slice adds persistence.
options.shows_it_works: Test loads docs sample JSON from disk, exports one SVG, edits a position, and re-exports showing the change in markup.
options.grounded_in: documentation/docs/requirements.md:1, quoted exactly above: 'The first board exports one SVG from local data.'

options.title: Local data is a JSON file and edits write back to it
options.description: Same load, plus a saveBoard(board) that serializes edits back to the local file, so defined editing has tangible persistence.
options.tradeoff: Editing becomes more 'real' (persistent), but write-back is not requested by any line in docs/, risks data loss on bad writes, and pre-decides how editing manifests without answering line 2's undecided interaction.
options.shows_it_works: Test loads, edits, saves, reloads from disk and asserts the edit survived round-trip.
options.grounded_in: documentation/docs/requirements.md:2, 'Editing is requested, but its interaction style is undecided.' — persistence is one interpretation of editing, chosen rather than derived; flagged as such.

options.title: Defer building until the interaction style is decided
options.description: Stop after reading docs/ and produce no slice until line 2 is answered, since editing could reshape data loading.
options.tradeoff: Avoids any rework risk, but line 1's slice is independently decidable ('The first board exports one SVG from local data.') and does not depend on how editing is interacted with; deferring blocks the named first slice without cause.
options.shows_it_works: Nothing to demonstrate; this option is a stop, which is a permitted outcome, just not required for line 1.

recommendation: Option A: it implements line 1 verbatim and parks line 2 as an explicit open decision rather than silently resolving it.
notes: The unresolved tension between the two lines is stated as the key decision question above. Nothing is approved, no person was consulted, and this is a proposal only.
